content.title: About
content.content: Vienna sausage, canned, is a ready‑to‑eat meat product made from finely ground pork and beef, seasoned with spices and flavorings. It is packed in a hermetically sealed metal can, providing a long shelf life without refrigeration.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original Vienna sausage was created in Austria at the end of the 19th century as a convenient snack for travelers.
Traditional recipes combine beef, pork, onion, salt, white pepper and paprika.
Cans are often coated with a lacquer layer to prevent corrosion and preserve flavor.
Vienna sausage is popular in many post‑Soviet countries, where it is used in salads, sandwiches and hot dishes.
There are nitrite‑free versions aimed at consumers who avoid artificial preservatives.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The sausage provides about 12–14 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Typically less than 2 g of carbs per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Convenient and long‑lasting
items.content: The sealed can allows storage for 2–3 years without refrigeration.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Vienna sausage is fairly salty (about 1.5 g of salt per 100 g), so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Some varieties contain nitrites, which may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Contains 20–25 g of fat per 100 g, including saturated fatty acids.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to pork or beef may experience reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sausage can be eaten straight from the can, warmed in the microwave or skillet, added to salads, pasta, omelets, or used as a sandwich filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the contents in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3–5 days.
